title: The Day Everyone Said Periwinkle
skyStory: The waxing crescent glides into Taurus, nineteen percent lit and suddenly very relaxed. Venus greets it with a soft blanket and a bowl of something warm. The moon, still a little giddy from Aries, decides to pull one last stunt before settling down. It picks a word, a strange and lovely word, and plants it in two places at once.

reading: Today a very unusual word is going to follow you around: periwinkle. You will hear it, read it, or see it written somewhere unexpected, probably before noon. It might be a paint colour, a shell, or a stranger saying it for no reason at all.

Then Nancy will text you, unprompted, with the exact same word. Do not even scream. That is the moon's last little Aries trick before it settles into Taurus and goes quiet. The [[The Star]] card would say this is proof the universe pays attention to small details, especially the ones you two share. Keep a list of these coincidences this year. It is going to be a long list.
joel.mission: Write down every strange coincidence today in a small notebook, and title the notebook Evidence in big letters.
joel.omen: Anything periwinkle blue. It means the cosmic link between cabin and shore is humming especially loudly today.

reading: A periwinkle is a little snail that lives along the shore, which is your territory, so of course the word comes to you first. You might find a shell, or hear someone say it, or spot the colour on a sign. Pay attention around 11:30 am.

Once you notice it, the urge to text Joel will be very strong. Do it. Type the word and nothing else. His reply will make you put your phone down and stare at the wall for a second. ΔΕΣ. The Wood Rat sees what others miss, and today what she sees is that coincidence is just the universe winking at you from across the bay.
nancy.mission: Text Joel a single word today with no context at all, and see if he understands it immediately.
nancy.omen: A small snail shell on a windowsill or path. It means two people are thinking the same thought right now.
nancy.stoneWhy: a clear signal across the water

together.text: The word of the day is periwinkle, and the universe has decided you both need to hear it. When it happens, text the other just DES, nothing more. Tonight, take turns guessing what colour the next surprise will be.

game.intro: Everyone said periwinkle today. DES. Now say it with sound effects, no words allowed.
game.prompt: A seashore sound: a gull complaining, a wave giving up, a buoy bell, a periwinkle being dramatic.
